Agent Standup turns your Claude Code session into a live team meeting: the lead gives orders, sub-agents join, share their screen and report back. It’s a bit silly. It’s also weirdly useful.

(An illustration. The real thing is live, has voices, and follows your actual session.)

reactions: [Hacker News] One useful part of standup is to elicit connections where one wasn't expected. For example, someone might say "I've been working on X" and another person might say "Oh, I worked on X a couple of days ago and you should know ..." It is an opportunity for things people didn't realize they needed to communicate to get stated publicly in a way that can create connect

[Hacker News] I'd instead say that for both it's really at 100%, and not any number in between. Problem is that we can't define precisely what is good enough or when software is "finished": I mean, we are trying to do that with human languages, so it should not be a surprise. Yes, LLMs are now similarly aware of the average context a human would be aware of, but for anything specific to

[Hacker News] That's why people "meet". However, a "standup" was invented to solve a particular problem: people, in isolation, do not always understand that they are stuck, and talking it through lets fellow humans identify their challenge. The stand up part is mostly to encourage keeping it concise and short, so you only focus on what is actionable between all participants (waiting on

[Hacker News] I don’t think it will disappear as the tools can be useful (finding bugs, searching large stores of info etc), but obviously bogus things like this meant to impress the gullible will disappear yes. Sadly the internet has already been ruined by bots pretending to be human, and there’s no way back from that.
[Hacker News] This makes me want to get a job just to be able to run this with my coworkers.
